newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK government paper dips on worries over U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: HK government paper dips on worries over U.S. data.

text.p: Long-end Hong Kong government paper prices weakened on Thursday in line with U.S. Treasuries while interbank rates were mixed, dealers said.
The seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.81 percent compared with Wednesday midday's 7.78. The five-year yielded 7.45 percent versus 7.42 and three-year was at 6.85 vs 6.82.
One-week bill yields, however, fell back to 4.98 percent from 5.10 percent.
Dealers said demand for longer term paper had tumbled as players held back fearing a possible hike in U.S. interest rates.
"U.S. payroll data will be out on Friday and people are fearing a subsequent rise in interest rates," said a dealer with a Japanese bank.
In the interbank market, short term rates eased as initial fears over the Iraqi crisis faded, while longer term money was steady, dealers said.
Overnight stood at 5-1/8 percent against 5-7/16 5/16 while three-month stood at 5-11/16 5/8 versus 5-11/16 9/16.
